## #10919: DateField and TimeField copy/paste

[PR](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10919), revision `c92cfdc57a90ae7d5be67714374e7f148b574b8c`. **High complexity:** new feature and public state API across RAC hooks, state, components/tests and docs; seven files, 648 additions and three deletions.

The change adds whole-value copy, ISO/current-locale paste and focused-segment numeric paste using `useClipboard`, with parsing in a new 296-line helper. It adds RAC component tests and documentation, but the clipboard contract still needs a team decision and the author has not signed the CLA.

**API and compatibility:** [diff](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10919/files), `packages/react-stately/src/datepicker/useDateFieldState.ts:134-138`, adds required public `DateFieldState.setFields(fields: DateFields & TimeFields): void`; custom state implementations can therefore face a structural type compatibility change. The implementation at `:429-441` applies several displayed segments and commits once. `packages/react-aria/src/datepicker/useDateSegment.ts:332-365` adds clipboard handlers to the existing segment props; copying any segment now copies the whole displayed value, and paste can replace the field or focused segment. This changes existing interaction behavior throughout consumers of the hooks, not just the two documented RAC components. No prop/default, DOM structure, class, data-attribute or CSS-variable change is apparent in this diff. Would apply `needs API review` for the state method and clipboard interaction contract.

**Direction/readiness:** the original [#5285 discussion](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5285#issuecomment-1799282356) says, "we will need to decide on a way forward and probably try to scope it down to something doable." The PR proposes ISO plus locale-format parsing, relaxed separators, time-zone conversion and whole-value copy without multi-segment selection. It acknowledges the shape of `setFields` is open to change. Would apply `needs decision`: is this precise format/selection/time-zone contract acceptable, and should bulk assignment be a public state method? Reid's [suggestion to use `useClipboard`](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5285#issuecomment-1799076827) and [support for the enhancement in #5364](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5364#issuecomment-1799030195) establish interest, not agreement on all of this behavior.

The [checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10919/checks) show Adobe CLA `ACTION_REQUIRED`, while reported test/lint/types and aggregate commit contexts are successful. The body lists 30 new clipboard cases and verification instructions, but explicitly says it dispatched paste events from script rather than real Cmd+V and did not test Safari, Firefox, mobile or screen readers. Would require CLA completion and an agreed verification plan for native clipboard behavior before readiness. The body's four locally failing RSP date-picker tests are claimed to fail on main too; that attribution was not independently executed, and the green returned CI is the stronger available evidence. Per step 1, no full low-complexity red-flag or parser-correctness review was performed.

**Duplicates:** searches by #5285, date-field copy/paste behavior and the state filename found no competing implementation. [#5364](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5364) explicitly lists "It is not possible to copy & paste dates (#5285)" among several usability concerns: would link it as related, not close the whole issue or call it a duplicate PR. [#10153](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10153) is the merged hooks-docs work, not a replacement. The known-format userland approach suggested [here](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5285#issuecomment-2601059886) is evidence of a constrained alternative, but its contributor-supplied sandbox was not opened or validated; would not assert it solves the general request.

**Would have done**

- **Labels:** would apply `merge-risk: high` for a broad clipboard feature and new required state method; `ai-reviewed` for completed scoped triage; `needs API review` for `setFields` and interaction compatibility; `needs decision` for the format/selection/time-zone contract; `waiting for author` for the unsigned CLA and native-clipboard verification gap. Remove: none.
- **Ready for review:** Would have added `ready for review`: no. Missing signed CLA, agreement on the clipboard/API contract, and native clipboard verification appropriate to the agreed scope.
- **Comment:** no comment.
- **Close / link:** would not close; would link #5285 and #5364 as related feature context. No competing PR to prefer.
- **Other:** would escalate the contract to devongovett/reidbarber for API and product-direction review; no assignment proposed.
- **Confidence:** high on CLA/API/direction blockers, medium on merge risk; signed CLA, an agreed contract and cross-browser native-clipboard evidence would change readiness.
- **Feedback prompt:** Review whether the proposed locale/ISO parsing and whole-value-copy contract is the scope the team wants.

## #10914: Parcel 3 alpha upgrade

[PR](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10914), revision `c79fc1414ecc89cb4094ad35f251df394051713b`. **Medium complexity:** 19 files across dependencies, docs runtime, stories and internal AI-component utilities; 238 additions and 194 deletions. This is an existing-toolchain upgrade with internal refactoring, not a new library feature.

The PR upgrades Parcel 3 and its Storybook/docs transformers, adapts docs loading/rendering and extracts MIME utilities to remove an AI-component import cycle. The description is empty, and the changed RSC dependency has a peer-version mismatch that needs resolution or a justified compatibility explanation.

**API and compatibility:** [diff](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10914/files), `package.json:115` upgrades `@parcel/parcel3` from `^0.0.6` to `^3.0.0-alpha.1`; the transformer dependency hunks upgrade `@parcel/transformer-storybook-v3` and `@parcel/transformer-ts-doc` to `^0.0.3`, and the resolutions hunk removes the RSC canary override. `packages/dev/parcel-transformer-intl/package.json:11` widens supported Parcel engines to `^2.0.0 || ^3.0.0-0`. `yarn.lock` changes `react-server-dom-parcel` to `19.3.1`, requiring React and React DOM `^19.3.1`, while unchanged root `package.json:250,252` resolutions pin both to `19.3.0`. Would require compatible runtime versions or an explicit explanation; installation success alone does not establish RSC runtime compatibility.

The MIME helpers move from `PromptField.tsx` into `src/mimeType.ts`, with both consumers updated. They were not exported by the supported `exports/index.ts` entry point on main (`:7-21`), so the removed source-file exports do not establish a supported public API removal. `MessageSuggestion` exports are reordered, not removed. Docs `CodeBlock.tsx` changes how function-valued example exports are rendered, and import/JSON adaptation changes dev/docs behavior; no component prop/default/event, DOM-structure, public class/data-attribute or CSS-variable contract change is apparent. Would not apply library `needs API review` on the available evidence.

**Needs security review:** would escalate dependency and lockfile changes, native Parcel binary versions, RSC runtime changes and docs-server HMR configuration. This is the mandatory tooling/dependency flag, not a vulnerability finding. The [author's inline note](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10914#discussion_r4459757323) explains the utility extraction: "AttachmentList depending on PromptField created a circular dependency" and could change CSS order. The [JSON note](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10914#discussion_r4459769953) explains the Parcel 2/3 compatibility fallback; neither substitutes for a verification plan for the upgrade.

**Readiness:** [checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10914/checks) show signed CLA, green lint/tests/docs/build contexts, but `ci/circleci: ts-build-fork-point` and aggregate `commit` fail. The fork-point context may be a baseline problem; its reason was not retrievable through the permitted GitHub-only reads, so would not attribute it to the PR. Would apply `waiting for maintainer` to establish CI attribution and coordinate the tooling/security review, and `waiting for author` for the missing overall description/instructions and runtime compatibility explanation. The three self-review comments explain individual changes, not how to verify both Parcel modes and the docs-server changes. No full low-complexity red-flag review was performed.

**Duplicates:** [#10454](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10454), merged August 14 with signed CLA, introduced the opt-in Parcel 3 build; this is a later upgrade, not work already satisfied by it. [#10811](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10811), open with CLA `ACTION_REQUIRED`, ports the separate `packages/dev/parcel-transformer-storybook` to Storybook 11 and says to land with that upgrade. Shared root dependency/lockfile edits are coordination overlap, not equivalent changes; #10914 updates `@parcel/transformer-storybook-v3`, not that local transformer. Would retain both and link for toolchain coordination, without preferring the signed PR over an unrelated implementation. Recent-closed `parcel3` search also returned [#10819](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10819), a TabPanels measurement fix, not an alpha-upgrade candidate.

**Would have done**

- **Labels:** would apply `merge-risk: high` for dependency/native-binary/RSC compatibility exposure; `ai-reviewed` for scoped triage; `waiting for author` for description/instructions and the React/RSC mismatch; `waiting for maintainer` for CI failure attribution and tooling/security review. Remove: none.
- **Ready for review:** Would have added `ready for review`: no. Missing overall problem/verification instructions, compatible or justified React/RSC versions, and established CI-failure attribution.
- **Comment:** no comment.
- **Close / link:** would not close; would link #10811 for coordination and #10454 as upgrade history. No duplicate winner.
- **Other:** would escalate dependency/native-binary/docs-server changes for security review, with devongovett coordinating the upgrade. No assignment proposed.
- **Confidence:** high on dependency/peer-version evidence, medium on readiness; explicit compatibility evidence, instructions and baseline CI attribution would change the decision.
- **Feedback prompt:** Review whether the runtime peer mismatch is intentional and whether the upgrade has adequate Parcel 2/3 verification evidence.

## #10915: popup TimeField layout inside Form

[PR](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10915), revision `787adb2d41b665424a2a78352e96f6b630bf548d`. **Low complexity:** one shared S2 picker-popover implementation and two regression stories; 27 additions and one deletion. Would apply `small review` for the focused component fix, not as a claim of low risk.

**Issue verification/main:** [#10899](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10899) reports that a time-enabled RSP S2 DatePicker inside Form has a clipped popup TimeField, while replacing Form with a div avoids it. On main, `packages/@react-spectrum/s2/src/TimeField.tsx:81,93` derives `isInForm` from `FormContext`; `src/style-utils.ts:55-62` selects `gridTemplateColumns: 'subgrid'` in a form; `src/DatePicker.tsx:254-275,292-310` places the popup TimeField below flex layout while retaining that context. The [diff](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10915/files), `src/DatePicker.tsx:309-316`, clears `FormContext` inside the shared `CalendarPopover`, plausibly removing the inappropriate subgrid for both pickers. Main does not already contain that reset. No supported picker prop or documented styling/composition alternative preserving the original Form behavior was identified; replacing Form with a div changes the form contract and is not a general recommended workaround.

**API/compatibility concern:** the body explicitly says, "the popup time field no longer inherits the form's `validationBehavior`." Main's `packages/react-aria-components/src/DateField.tsx:235-242` confirms TimeField falls back from inherited form behavior to `'native'`. The popup fields do not receive an explicit `validationBehavior` in the main picker (`src/DatePicker.tsx:262-274`). This is a change to the behavior of an existing Form prop, not just visual repair. Would apply `needs API review` and `needs decision`: should popup fields lose inherited validation behavior, or should the layout fix preserve it? No public prop/export/default declaration or explicit DOM/class/data-attribute/CSS-variable change is introduced by the diff.

**Tests/discussion:** new `OpenPickerWithTimeInForm` chromatic stories for DatePicker (`:114-122`) and DateRangePicker (`:128-136`) inherit the existing opened-picker interaction and reproduce the reported layout. The author reports before/after widths of 4px versus normal widths, but these measurements were not independently executed. The [maintainer requested Chromatic VRT rather than a browser test](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10915#discussion_r4461458561), and the [author moved the test accordingly](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10915#discussion_r4462070292); the current diff supports that response. No violation of the linked issue discussion was found: its only comment is a contributor volunteering to investigate. There is no integration test of the changed `validationBehavior="aria"` semantics.

**Other low-complexity flags:** no new check suppression, timing hack, user-agent sniffing, DOM poking or removed ARIA/focus/keyboard support appears in the diff. Validation feedback is the accessibility/compatibility surface needing attention. [Checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10915/checks) show signed CLA and all returned contexts successful; the author says Chromatic was not run. Would not invent a `regression` or `patch worthy` recommendation without prior-working-version/release-policy evidence.

**Duplicates:** searches for #10899, DatePicker/Form behavior and `CalendarPopover` found no competing popup TimeField fix. Merged [#8621](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/8621) changes Calendar/RangeCalendar header rendering in a dialog, not FormContext or popup time-field sizing; would not treat it as a prior fix for this reproduction.

**Would have done**

- **Labels:** would apply `merge-risk: medium` for validation semantics changed by a visual fix; `ai-reviewed` for completed low-complexity triage; `small review` for the localized component change; `needs API review` for inherited Form validation compatibility; `needs decision` on preserving versus intentionally changing popup validation; `waiting for maintainer` for that decision and the next review pass. Remove: none.
- **Ready for review:** Would have added `ready for review`: no. Missing an agreed validation behavior and appropriate integration coverage if that behavior changes; CLA, description, visual stories and returned CI are otherwise satisfactory.
- **Comment:** no comment.
- **Close / link:** would not close; would link #10899 as the reproduction. No duplicate winner.
- **Other:** would escalate the validation compatibility question to snowystinger, who already reviewed the test placement; no assignment proposed.
- **Confidence:** high on the context/validation side effect, medium on readiness; confirmation that the behavior is intentional, with coverage, or preservation of existing validation would change the decision.

## #10916: stable list-formatter options

[PR](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10916), revision `fa64eb62008c086b8b0f5e236e626cefd1051585`. **Low complexity:** one utility hook, 22 added source lines, plus a 40-line hook test; no new feature or core date/collection/overlay behavior.

**Problem/main:** the body says "Closes: no matching issue found." Would flag the absence of a linked issue, but its clear explanation is enough to identify the claimed allocation problem. Main's `packages/react-aria/src/i18n/useListFormatter.tsx:22-24` depends on options object identity, so an inline/default options object recreates `Intl.ListFormat`. The [diff](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10916/files), `useListFormatter.tsx:14,24-47`, reuses value-equal options with the existing `useDeepMemo`, matching main `useDateFormatter.ts:28-52`. No issue reproduction or issue discussion exists to cross-check.

**Already solvable:** supported caller-side memoization prevents the same unnecessary allocations without changing the hook:

```tsx
const options = useMemo(() => ({type: 'conjunction'} as const), []);
const formatter = useListFormatter(options);
```

Main's hook depends on `[locale, options]`, so this still updates the formatter when the locale changes. The [main docs](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/6dec77beccf0545a04318e6a01b8eb9cbe2dccc6/packages/dev/s2-docs/pages/react-aria/useListFormatter.mdx#L24-L28) describe locale updates and performance caching, and `:40-44` uses inline options; the library fix would make that documented pattern more efficient. Would apply `has workaround` and `needs decision`: is removing the need for caller memoization worth the library change, with evidence of useful allocation reduction? The workaround does not establish that the PR is unnecessary.

**Tests/API:** `packages/react-aria/test/i18n/useListFormatter.test.js:17-39` asserts formatter identity across equal/default options and checks changed options produce `'a or b'`. By reading main, the equal/default identity assertions would fail before the change. Identity testing is relevant to this optimization, but most coverage is allocation/internal-return behavior rather than a realistic rendered consumer; locale-change coverage and demonstrated practical performance impact are absent. No prop/export/type/event/default, DOM/class/data-attribute or CSS-variable change is apparent. Returned formatter identity becomes more stable, which is the intended observable behavioral difference, not a breaking declaration change; would not apply `needs API review`.

**Other low-complexity flags/readiness:** no new suppression, timing hack, ARIA change, focus manipulation or browser workaround appears in the diff. The reused `useDeepMemo` has existing lint suppressions on main, not new suppressions in this PR. [Checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10916/checks) show CLA `ACTION_REQUIRED`, `ci/circleci: lint` failure and aggregate commit failure, while returned tests and types are green. The author says Node/Yarn were unavailable for local execution. Would require the author to sign the CLA and resolve or explain the lint failure; its exact cause could not be read through permitted GitHub-only APIs, so no diagnostic is guessed.

**Duplicates:** [#10879](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10879), also open and unsigned, uses the same optimization pattern for `useNumberFormatter`, but changes distinct source/test files and a different formatter. Would retain both as related work, not draft a duplicate notice or select a winner; neither has a CLA advantage. Searches for list formatter/options behavior and the exact filename found no competing list-formatter implementation. Main contains the date-formatter prior art, not this list-formatter fix.

**Would have done**

- **Labels:** would apply `merge-risk: medium` for failed lint and practical/locale verification gaps; `ai-reviewed` for completed low-complexity triage; `small review` for one localized utility; `waiting for author` for unsigned CLA and lint resolution/explanation; `has workaround` for supported stable options; `needs decision` on the usefulness of library-level allocation stabilization versus caller memoization. Remove: none.
- **Ready for review:** Would have added `ready for review`: no. Missing signed CLA, resolved/explained lint failure and a decision on the optimization's necessity/verification. No linked issue, though the body explains the problem.
- **Comment:** no comment.
- **Close / link:** would not close; would link #10879 for optimization-pattern coordination, not as a duplicate.
- **Other:** would seek maintainer judgment on realistic rerender/locale coverage and performance evidence; no assignment proposed.
- **Confidence:** high on CLA/lint/workaround evidence, medium on whether this change is worth adopting; signed CLA, lint attribution and practical evidence would change readiness.
- **Feedback prompt:** Review whether this allocation-only optimization needs additional consumer/performance evidence or is justified by the existing date-formatter precedent.

## #10921: allow Escape through a closed PreviewTrigger

[PR](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10921), revision `090040021579ec6bc5e95e9e7808e8d9c3e614ac`. **Low complexity:** one component-specific keyboard branch plus one rendered RAC regression assertion; four additions and one deletion. The small single-component bug-fix criterion takes precedence over the general shared-hook rule here.

**Issue verification/main:** [#10918](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10918) describes first closing a preview with Escape, then pressing Escape on the focused trigger to close a containing popup whose handler ignores `defaultPrevented` events. Main's `packages/react-aria/src/tooltip/usePreviewTrigger.ts:179-182` always prevents Escape. The [diff](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10921/files), `usePreviewTrigger.ts:179-185`, prevents it only while `state.isOpen` but retains `state.close(true)`. That plausibly fixes the second-Escape cancellation without weakening first-Escape handling or removing the existing close call. The issue has no comments, so there is no maintainer direction to contradict.

**Existing solutions:** main still contains the unconditional prevention; the [docs](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/6dec77beccf0545a04318e6a01b8eb9cbe2dccc6/packages/dev/s2-docs/pages/react-aria/PreviewTrigger.mdx#L122-L128) describe Escape closing the preview but expose no documented switch to stop this closed-state interception. The issue's stop/re-dispatch workaround is a DOM/event hack, not a recommended accessible composition solution. No supported equivalent fix was identified.

**Tests/API/accessibility:** `packages/react-aria-components/test/PreviewTrigger.test.js:223` adds `expect(fireEvent.keyDown(link, {key: 'Escape'})).toBe(true)` after the existing rendered test closes the preview and confirms restored focus. A cancelable keydown's return value directly checks the erroneous `preventDefault`; by reading main this assertion would fail before the change. This is rendered-component event behavior, not a private-state/call-count assertion, but it does not render the actual enclosing dialog or cover a trigger whose preview was never opened. Would accept it for this narrow cancellation fix while recording that integration gap. The existing test remains an instruction for tabbing into a preview, closing it and restoring focus; the issue supplies the enclosing-handler scenario.

No new prop/export/type/default, DOM structure, class/data-attribute/CSS-variable change is apparent. Closed-state Escape event cancellation changes intentionally; open-state handling, ARIA and focus restoration remain present. No new check suppression, timing hack, user-agent sniffing or DOM workaround appears in the diff. [Checks](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10921/checks) show signed CLA and all returned contexts successful. The issue reports the same problem in versions 3.52.1 and 3.53.1, not a previously working version, so would not label it `regression`; no patch-release recommendation without policy evidence.

**Duplicates:** searches for #10918, PreviewTrigger/Escape behavior and `usePreviewTrigger.ts` found only this direct fix plus related history. [#10696](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10696), open with signed CLA, restores default-open overlays from body focus using FocusScope/useOverlayTrigger and different tests; it does not change PreviewTrigger's closed-state Escape cancellation. Would retain both; neither has a CLA advantage. [#10243](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10243) is the original PreviewTrigger feature, not a competing fix, and [#10777](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10777) requests touch activation on press, not Escape handling.

**Would have done**

- **Labels:** would apply `merge-risk: low` for a narrow cancellation fix with rendered regression coverage and successful returned CI; `ai-reviewed` for completed low-complexity triage; `small review` for the focused component change; `ready for review` because no mandatory author blocker or direction dispute was identified. Remove: none.
- **Ready for review:** Would have added `ready for review`: yes. Signed CLA, clear linked reproduction, targeted rendered test and successful returned CI; enclosing-dialog/never-opened-trigger coverage remains a disclosed reviewer consideration, not a blocking failure.
- **Comment:** no comment.
- **Close / link:** would not close; would link #10918 as the reproduction and #10696 only as related focus work. No duplicate winner.
- **Other:** none; no assignment or escalation proposed.
- **Confidence:** medium; enclosing-dialog and never-opened-trigger tests, plus native keyboard verification, would increase confidence or reveal a reason to change readiness.
- **Feedback prompt:** Review whether the rendered cancellation assertion is sufficient, or whether the actual parent-popup interaction should block readiness.

## Rule feedback

- **Team decisions, listed separately:** #10919 needs an agreed clipboard format/selection/time-zone contract and public bulk-state API; #10915 needs a decision on preserving inherited validation behavior; #10916 needs a decision on library-level optimization versus a supported caller workaround. No evidence says these should simply be rejected or closed.
- **Complexity ambiguity:** the low-complexity single-component-fix criterion overlaps with high-complexity core-hook behavior changes. #10921 is treated as low because only a component-specific Escape cancellation condition changes; #10916 is a contained allocation optimization rather than core behavior. #10915's small context reset remains low in complexity but medium in risk because of its validation effect.
- **Medium/high review boundary:** #10919 and #10914 received classification, two-sentence summaries, API/compatibility and duplicate assessment, plus mandatory readiness/CLA/tooling checks. No full low-complexity red-flag review or parser/security audit was inferred.
- **Evidence limits:** PR code, tests, repros and contributor links were not run/opened. #10899's linked image and StackBlitz were not fetched under the stricter GitHub-read-only/contributor-URL restriction; layout was assessed from issue text and main/diff evidence. Native clipboard and enclosing-dialog behavior remain unverified locally. CLA/CI statuses are snapshots, not independently reproduced results.
- **CI attribution:** #10914's failing fork-point context may be baseline-related; #10916's failed lint has no diagnostic available in the returned GitHub metadata. CircleCI URLs were not opened or queried. Readiness is withheld rather than guessing blame or treating failures as green.
- **Search limits:** repository-qualified multiword `gh search` input initially produced invalid queries; retried with `--repo` and cross-checked through GET search API queries. Searches included issue numbers, behavior, exact filename mentions and related open/recently closed PRs. Filename text search does not index every changed-file list, so absence of a duplicate is bounded search evidence, not exhaustive proof. Broad historical Parcel search had 42 results and a 30-item page; focused Parcel 3 and recent-closed searches supplemented it.
- **Recovered read failures:** `gh pr diff 10914 --stat` failed because this gh version has no `--stat`; replaced with supported diff and API file/patch reads.
